display_name: Harivarma & Krishnavarma II of the Kadambas
one_line: Last independent Kadamba rulers of Banavasi and Triparvatha, holding the line in northern Karnataka just before the rise of the Badami Chalukyas.

appearance.age_look: Harivarma appears in his late 30s, lean and sharp; Krishnavarma II in his early 30s, slightly broader-shouldered and athletic.
appearance.face: Both have oval faces with medium-brown Deccan complexions; Harivarma has a narrower jaw, faint worry lines and a focused, serious default expression, while Krishnavarma has a squarer jaw, a small nose scar on the left bridge and a determined, confident default expression with intense eyes.
appearance.hair: Harivarma’s hair is dark brown, shoulder-length and wavy, parted at the center and drawn back into a low knot with a thin gold band around his forehead; Krishnavarma II’s hair is black, slightly shorter and tied into a high warrior topknot, held by a plain bronze circlet with a tiny central leaf motif.
appearance.costume: Both wear early 6th-century Deccan royal attire: Harivarma in a rich deep-maroon silk ankle-length dhoti with a narrow mustard border, pleated neatly at the front and tied high at the waist, a fitted short-sleeved cream-colored cotton tunic reaching mid-thigh with a subtle woven grid pattern, and a diagonal golden-yellow silk uttariya draped from his left shoulder across the chest to the right hip; Krishnavarma II in a forest-green cotton dhoti with a broad white border and front-knot, a sleeveless light-beige cotton angarkha-style vest wrapping left-over-right with a tied side-knot, and a sky-blue uttariya slung over both shoulders and falling behind like a short cape; both wear simple leather sandals, multiple gold and bronze bangles, a broad gold neck torque with small leaf pendants, modest ear ornaments (Harivarma small round studs, Krishnavarma short dangling hoops), and a narrow fabric kamarband—Harivarma’s red with tiny white dots, Krishnavarma’s dark blue with a chevron pattern.
appearance.signature: A single broad-bladed early-6th-century Deccan sword (slightly curved, about thigh-length) with a simple iron blade, a bronze cross-guard, a dark-brown wrapped leather hilt and a plain wooden scabbard painted deep red with a thin white line near the opening, hanging from Krishnavarma’s right hip on a brown leather belt while Harivarma’s right hand rests lightly on the scabbard to show shared authority.

ref_desc: Two medium-brown Deccan princes stand together: Harivarma in deep-maroon dhoti, cream tunic and golden-yellow uttariya with low-knot dark-brown hair and gold headband, Krishnavarma II in forest-green dhoti, beige vest, sky-blue uttariya, black topknot with bronze circlet, sharing one red-sheathed curved sword at Krishnavarma’s hip.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two early-6th-century Kadamba princes from northern Karnataka shown side by side, designed to be redrawn consistently: Harivarma is a lean man in his late 30s with an oval face, medium-brown Deccan complexion, thoughtful serious expression, and dark-brown wavy hair to the shoulders pulled back into a low knot, held by a thin gold band around his forehead; he wears a rich deep-maroon silk ankle-length dhoti with a narrow mustard border, pleated neatly, a fitted short-sleeved cream-colored cotton tunic with a subtle woven grid pattern reaching mid-thigh, a diagonal golden-yellow silk uttariya draped from his left shoulder across his chest to his right hip, a red kamarband with tiny white dots, gold and bronze bangles, a broad gold neck torque with small leaf pendants, small round gold ear studs, and simple leather sandals. Beside him, Krishnavarma II appears in his early 30s, slightly broader-shouldered with a squarer jaw, medium-brown complexion, a small scar on the left side of his nose bridge, and a confident determined expression; his black hair is tied into a high warrior topknot held by a plain bronze circlet with a tiny central leaf motif. He wears a forest-green cotton dhoti with a broad white border, knotted in front, a sleeveless light-beige cotton angarkha-style vest wrapping left-over-right with a side tie, a sky-blue uttariya draped over both shoulders and hanging behind like a short cape, a dark-blue chevron-patterned kamarband, modest short dangling hoop earrings, matching bangles, and simple leather sandals. At Krishnavarma’s right hip hangs their shared signature weapon, a slightly curved early-Deccan sword with an iron blade, bronze cross-guard, dark-brown wrapped leather hilt, and a plain wooden scabbard painted deep red with a thin white line near the opening, on a brown leather belt, while Harivarma’s right hand rests lightly on the scabbard to show their joint authority; keep the colour palette dominated by deep maroon, forest green, golden yellow, sky blue, and cream, and show them front-facing with clear views of face, hair, clothing, jewellery, and the sword for consistent character design.
